scientific.name: Sestrimo normal fault
scientific.system: North Rhodopean Extensional System / Kostenets-Sestrimo basin

notes: Kounov et al. describe the Sestrimo fault as Miocene-Quaternary normal faulting related to development of the Kostenets-Sestrimo basin.
Scientific Fig. 3 normal-fault baseline was reconstructed from vector primitives.
Reconstructed baseline: 35 points; distance to REC103 min 415.4 m, mean 635.8 m, max 936.9 m; all 35 points within 1 km.
REC103 is therefore the strongest MRRB local corridor correspondence, but is not treated as an identical one-to-one trace.

scientific.system: Upper Thracian Rift System / Belovo-Septemvri-Pazardzhik fault network

notes: Popov et al. 2015 describe numerous faults most likely developed from the Belovo and Septemvri areas toward Pazardzhik beneath Quaternary sediments.
K-35-061 supports a segmented structural/fault network rather than one continuous exact fault trace along REC79.
REC79 is approximately parallel to REC18 Belovo but is retained as a separate MRRB corridor.
EUR_BGCS005 is the nearest GEM/BGCS modeled source at approximately 2267.5 m from REC79 and does not intersect the MRRB corridor; no BGCS crosswalk is assigned.
EUR_BGCS027 is approximately 7744.1 m from REC79 and also does not intersect.

scientific.system: North Rhodopean fault system / southern Upper Thracian basin-margin faulting

notes: REC15 is the nearest MRRB corridor for 83.35 percent of EUR_BGCS046 and for 72.13 percent of the modeled source within a 2 km proximity threshold.
The main REC15 and BGCS046 axes differ by approximately 6.58 degrees.

Dense ownership analysis identifies two major REC15-controlled BGCS046 intervals of approximately 30.97 km and 17.38 km; the eastern end is locally closer to REC121 Novakovo and a short intermediate interval to REC122 Stamboliyski.
Popov et al. 2015 describe the North Rhodopean fault as the best expressed structure separating the Upper Thracian Rift System from the northern Rhodope slopes between Belovo and Asenovgrad.

Affine georeferencing of Popov et al. 2015 Fig. 3 produced 3.25 px RMS and 5.286 px maximum control residual; BGCS046 follows the same southern basin-margin fault belt but corresponds to several established fault segments rather than one exact mapped trace.
BGCS046 is not identified with the historical dextral Maritsa strike-slip fault system; Gerdjikov and Georgiev 2006 state that modern activity of that strike-slip system is not demonstrated.
open_items: Exact one-to-one scientific fault name remains unresolved; North Rhodopean fault system is retained as the regional scientific system rather than exact trace identity.

scientific.system: Upper Thracian Rift System / Peshtera-Bratsigovo lineament and fault network

notes: REC76 is a 13.067 km low-class MRRB corridor with an approximately east-west PCA strike of 93.05 degrees.
Affine georeferencing of Popov et al. 2015 Fig. 3 produced 3.25 px RMS and 5.286 px maximum control residual.

A reconstructed REC76 corridor centreline differs from the MRRB length by only 0.74 percent; 75.45 percent of its samples lie within 5 px and 93.81 percent within 10 px of the red ASTER-interpreted lineament network.
Correspondence to the orange faults established from field, well and seismic-geophysical evidence is substantially weaker: 7.19 percent within 5 px and 17.76 percent within 10 px.
Geological map K-35-061 does not show one continuous east-west mapped fault along REC76; the corridor crosses oblique mapped structures and is not assigned an exact geological-map trace.
No GEM/BGCS source intersects REC76. EUR_BGCS005 is nearest at approximately 3353.5 m, followed by EUR_BGCS029 at 7041.5 m and EUR_BGCS046 at 14194.6 m; no BGCS crosswalk is assigned.
REC122 Stamboliyski is the nearest MRRB corridor at approximately 4816.8 m and has a similar regional orientation, but the two corridors remain separate and are not merged.

Kounov et al. 2023 place the ancient Izvor-Peshtera Basin in the hanging wall of the North Rhodopean Detachment, but that detachment became inactive in the early Oligocene and is not used as a modern REC76 identity.

scientific.system: Upper Thracian Rift System / southern basin-margin lineament and fault network

notes: REC122 is a 29.100 km medium-class MRRB corridor with a PCA strike of approximately 98.84 degrees.
Affine georeferencing of Popov et al. 2015 Fig. 3 produced 3.25 px RMS and 5.286 px maximum control residual.

A reconstructed REC122 corridor centreline differs from the MRRB length by only 0.33 percent; 74.45 percent of its samples lie within 5 px and 93.21 percent within 10 px of the red ASTER-interpreted lineament network.
Correspondence to the orange faults established from field, well and seismic-geophysical evidence is weak: 0 percent within 5 px, 4.79 percent within 10 px and 14.97 percent within 20 px.

No GEM/BGCS modeled source intersects REC122. EUR_BGCS005 is nearest at approximately 381.3 m from the western end, while EUR_BGCS046 is approximately 1017.3 m from the eastern part; no BGCS crosswalk is assigned.

REC122 is the nearest MRRB owner for the final approximately 2.989 km of EUR_BGCS005, but the median separation is approximately 1864.1 m and only 0.20 percent of the full modeled source is both REC122-owned and within 500 m.

REC122 is the nearest MRRB owner for approximately 2.176 km of EUR_BGCS046, but that interval remains approximately 1017.3 to 1478.6 m away and has a local orientation difference of approximately 28.55 degrees.
REC76 Peshtera is the nearest MRRB corridor at approximately 4816.8 m and has a similar regional orientation, but REC76 and REC122 remain separate and are not merged.

scientific.system: North Rhodopean fault system / southern Upper Thracian basin-margin faulting

notes: REC121 is an 8.667 km medium-class MRRB corridor with a PCA strike of approximately 97.80 degrees.
Affine georeferencing of Popov et al. 2015 Fig. 3 produced 3.25 px RMS and 5.286 px maximum control residual.

A reconstructed REC121 corridor centreline differs from the MRRB length by 1.11 percent; 43.71 percent of its samples lie within 5 px and 67.47 percent within 10 px of the red ASTER-interpreted lineament network.
Correspondence to the orange faults established from field, well and seismic-geophysical evidence is limited: 19.56 percent within 5 px, 25.55 percent within 10 px and 36.13 percent within 20 px.
EUR_BGCS046 intersects REC121 for only approximately 160.7 m, representing about 0.277 percent of the modeled source.
REC121 is the nearest MRRB owner for the final approximately 7.457 km or 12.87 percent of EUR_BGCS046, but the median separation within that interval is approximately 1029.1 m.
Only 3.12 percent of the full EUR_BGCS046 source is both REC121-owned and within 500 m of the corridor; the local REC121-BGCS046 orientation difference is approximately 20.54 degrees.
EUR_BGCS046 is retained as a MEDIUM spatial relation rather than a partial or exact trace crosswalk, and its normal-fault kinematics are not inherited by REC121.

scientific.name: South Ihtiman normal fault
scientific.system: Maritsa fault system / southern Ihtiman basin margin

notes: REC17 is a 39.636 km high-class MRRB corridor with a PCA strike of approximately 120.21 degrees.
EUR_BGCS027 intersects REC17 for approximately 1273.1 m, representing about 2.804 percent of the modeled source; the local orientation difference at the nearest sector is approximately 0.01 degrees.
REC17 is the nearest MRRB owner for approximately 90.63 percent or 41.142 km of EUR_BGCS027; 75.48 percent of the complete modeled source lies within 1 km of REC17.

Radulov et al. 2015 identify the South Ihtiman fault as a mountain-bounding normal fault along the northeastern Cherni Rid foothill that controls Neogene-Quaternary deposition in the Ihtiman basin; its mapped length is 18.35 +/- 0.95 km.
The Radulov et al. paleoseismic trench at 23.73317861 E, 42.41691889 N lies approximately 716.6 m outside REC17 but only approximately 118.1 m from EUR_BGCS027.

Affine georeferencing of geological map K-34-060 Ihtiman produced 26.104 px RMS and 38.995 px maximum control residual; the overlay supports a shared southern basin-margin structural belt but is not accurate enough for exact trace identity.
REC17 is substantially longer than the published 18.35 km South Ihtiman fault and is therefore retained as a partial local scientific correspondence rather than a one-to-one fault trace.

The normal-fault kinematics of the scientific South Ihtiman fault and EUR_BGCS027 are consistent with the regional relation, but the MRRB polygon remains an official hazard corridor rather than the scientific surface trace.
